findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a significant accumulation of soil debris on the soda nozzles at the server station. CORRECTED- nozzles were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Discussed more intensive cleaning process than soaking overnight moving forward. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the fans of the walk in cooler contain an accumulation of dust. Dust may travel to contaminate nonfood and food contact surfaces. Ensure these items are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.  [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a significant accumulation of soil debris on the soda nozzles at both the grill and server station. CORRECTED- nozzles were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Discussed more intensive cleaning process than soaking overnight moving forward. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf[

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed plates in the grill and assisted living area facing upwards without a covering. CORRECTED- plates were moved under a covering or inverted. Ensure food contact surfaces are protected from contamination by storing inverted or under a covering.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following physical facilities in need of cleaning or repair:
1) The caulking to the right of the kitchen’s dish machine is separating. Reseal to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
2) The fans of the walk in cooler contain an accumulation of dust. Dust may travel to contamination nonfood and food contact surfaces.
Ensure these items are cleaned and repaired by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the handwashing sink in the Assisted Living Dining Room being used as a dump sink. CORRECTED- Education occurred between the inspector and Person in Charge (PIC). Handwashing sinks are to be used only for hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw chicken being stored over raw ground beef in a cooler (to the left of the handwashing sink) in the Grill area of the facility. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the chicken to be stored on the bottom shelf, and notified staff that animal proteins should be stored so that items requiring higher internal temperatures for cooking are stored below other items (proteins requiring a lower internal temperature and ready to eat [RTE] foods). Ensure storage order education occurs with all food handlers on a routine basis.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The saniziter bucket in the main kitchen was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- kitchen staff remade sanitizer bucket to an acceptable value (200 ppm quaternary ammonia). Ensure sanitizer buckets are made and checked (using facility’s test strips) at a frequency to maintain the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed breakage in the gaskets of the main kitchen’s standing freezer (to the left of the hood vent system). Inspector showed the PIC the gaskets, which they added to their repair order list. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Slight soil accumulation was observed in the main kitchen ice machine. Ensure the interiors of ice machines are cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. [C]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Single service containers on the main kitchen cookline were observed stored with food-contact surfaces up, exposed to potential contamination from above. Store single-service containers inverted to prevent potential contamination of the food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

findings.comment:
No paper towels were available at the wait station handsink. The battery in the paper towel dispenser was dead. CORRECTED- Batteries were changed and the dispenser was observed to function properly. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.comment:
An ice cream scoop was observed in the wait station handsink. CORRECTED- Scoop was removed and sink was cleaned. Ensure handwashing sinks are only used for handwashing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Cooling portion of cheese sauce observed in a small prep cooler without time noted or any additional cooling methods in use. CORRECTED- Sauce was placed in an ice bath and moved to the walk-in cooler to cool.
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [Pf]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Forks and spoons observed at the assisted living service counter with food contact ends out. CORRECTED- Utensils were rearranged to protect the food contact ends. 
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 A cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Ensure staff are was using proper technique when washing their hands.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Soap dispenser at server area handwashing sink was not working properly. Dispenser is designed to be automatic and/or manually dispense. It took several attempts to get a negligible amount of soap to dispense. PIC had maintenance replace the soap dispenser during inspection. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 1. Quat solution at 3 part sink was observed at 0ppm. Solution was remade and observed at 150-200ppm.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14 The following were all observed in the walk-in cooler.
1. Three containers of chicken and wild rice soup (~2.5gal each) made today were observed with internal temperatures of 49F, 45F, and 43F within the liquid portion of the soup (meat, vegetables, and rice settled to bottom). Based on cooling log, soup was prepared in the morning, had an internal temperature of 132F at 8am, and reached 51F after 2hrs. Based on the time frame of initial prep, the soup was past the 6hr time frame for proper cooling. Soup at 49F was discarded. 
2. Baking sheet with cooked rice had surface and internal temperature of 53F-62F and 61F-75F respectively. Cook stated rice was prepared around 11:30am-12pm. The first two hours of the cooling time frame was past based on information provided. Rice was discarded.
3. Cooked, shredded chicken in a covered container was observed with an internal temperature of 66F-67F. Cook noted it was cool to the touch when shredded and made around the same time as rice. Temperature was not monitored during the process. Chicken was discarded at the discretion of PIC.
Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled within 2 hours from 135F to 70F and within an additional 4 hours from 70F to 41F/below. Foods must be cooled in a total of 6 hours from 135F to 41F/below. 
Monitor the temperature of cooling foods with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are reaching bench mark temperatures in the designated time frames for proper cooling.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.11 Ice cream scoop available for use at AL dining area was observed to be rough and somewhat corroded. Scoop was removed for discard and replaced with a scoop that was in good repair. 
Multiuse food-contact surfaces shall be smooth and free of of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, inclusions, pits, and similar imperfections.

findings.citation_text:

2. Floor drain under the sprayer sink in the dish area was soiled with buildup, especially on the cover.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 1. Quat solution in sani-bucket at middle prep area was observed at a concentration below 100ppm. New solution was provided and observed at a concentration of 100ppm. Dispenser by mopsink used to fill buckets was checked to verify proper function. Freshly dispensed solution was observed at 400ppm. New solution was provided at proper concentration. Allow the sanitizer dispenser to run for several seconds prior to filling sanitizer-buckets and ensure sanitizer is suctioning properly through chemical line. Use test strips to verify concentration.

2. Quat solution at 3 part sink in dish area was observed at 100ppm. Solution was prepared a few hours prior and was in need of changing. Solution was discarded and fresh solution at 200ppm was provided.  

A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 A knife soiled with stuck on food debris was observed on top of the salad cooler and assumed to be left from operations the previous evening. Knife was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12 Inner surfaces of microwave were soiled with buildup of food splash. Cleaning frequency was discussed 
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice scoop holders in the server area were soiled with buildup in the bottom. Scoops and holders were taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, utensils such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Green slated shelving units used for storage of clean equipment had varying amounts of dust accumulation. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Clean equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee in dish area went from handling soiled dishes to putting away clean dishes without a hand wash in between. The employee also had a general wiping cloth that was used to wipe hands and then placed on their shoulder. Handwashing between tasks was discussed, and the wiping cloth was placed in the soiled linen storage at request of inspector. Employee was observed washing hands as needed between handling soiled and clean dishes for remainder of inspection. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, between handling soiled and clean equipment and utensils, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towel dispenser was empty at the AL kitchen. Paper towels were provided. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee was observed adjusting face mask with gloved hands prior to handling spice containers for prep. Proper use of gloves was discussed, and gloves were discarded. Ensure proper glove use. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.citation_text:

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certification was not available for one of the kitchen employees that has not yet completed the food manager certification. Proof of food handler certificaiton is required until food manger certification is completed. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Server in AL dining area picked up a glove that was dropped on the floor using a soiled wiping cloth. Server was wearing a glove on the other hand and proceeded to put on another glove without re-washing hands. Handwashing between tasks and after touching soiled surfaces/general debris were discussed. Server re-washed hands at the AL kitchen handsink prior to putting on a new pair of gloves to continue with the next task. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles and, before putting on gloves, between glove changes, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handsinks in a couple locations appeared to be used for tasks other than handwashing based on debris observed in the drains. Water was not draining properly at the AL kitchen handsink after use. A chunk of food debris that appeared to be pineapple and a leaf were observed in the drain. Debris was removed and water drained properly. Main kitchen handsink across from sautee and grill line was observed with significant sized chunks of food debris in the drain as well. Food debris was removed from the drain. PIC was advised to speak with staff and reiterate proper use of hansinks.   
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Handsinks should never be used as a dump sink or a location for rinsing dishes.
